title: Nvidia says its open-source AI strategy remains intact after Jensen Huang’s exit
content:
Nvidia interim CEO Collette Kress reaffirmed the company’s commitment to open-source AI during Tuesday’s earnings call with analysts — the first since CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation.
“At Nvidia, we are committed to fostering a vibrant open model ecosystem, so every country, company, and industry can build its own intelligence,” Kress said in her opening remarks. She also noted that open models were accelerating AI adoption, citing a 35-fold year-over-year surge in weekly token volume on OpenRouter, including a 3.5-fold increase over the past three months.
Kress also spoke about Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face, a platform for open-source AI models that the company agreed to acquire for $12.9 billion in September, in what would be the second-largest acquisition in Nvidia’s history.
The platform, which serves more than 118 million developers and 200,000 companies, is still on track to join Nvidia, despite Huang’s ouster. Huang had heavily advocated for open-source AI technology. His departure had raised questions about the company’s future approach to open-source AI models, with Hugging Face’s CEO called Huang’s departure “a sad day,” and promised to “keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever.”
So far, Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face appear unchanged. The acquisition was not directly addressed during the Q&A portion of the earnings call.
“Together, we will scale its platform and make intelligence more open, more capable, and more accessible,” said Kress of Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face.
Last week, Nvidia founder Huang resigned from his position as CEO following news about his extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang, an executive at the Singapore-based company Megaspeed who is suspected of being a Chinese spy. He’s also accused of having extramarital affairs with two direct reports and is now set to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving. Meanwhile, the SEC is investigating Nvidia over whether the company’s disclosures misled investors, The WSJ reported.
Within Nvidia, Huang pushed for the development of the Nemotron family of open-weight AI models built for long-running agentic AI systems and reasoning workloads. On today’s call, Kress noted that Nemotron is now the “most widely used U.S. open model on OpenRouter,” and it’s “where developers start to build their own intelligence.”
“That foundation is empowering the ecosystem,” she said.

report.summary: Nvidia’s interim CEO says the company’s open-source AI strategy and $12.9B Hugging Face acquisition remain on track after Jensen Huang’s resignation.
report.background: Jensen Huang had made open-source AI a pillar of Nvidia’s strategy, championing the Nemotron family of open-weight models and pushing the $12.9 billion acquisition of Hugging Face, agreed in September. Hugging Face serves more than 118 million developers and 200,000 companies, making the deal central to Nvidia’s effort to shape model distribution and inference demand. Huang resigned last week after disclosures about extramarital affairs, including a relationship with an executive suspected of being a Chinese spy, and he faces congressional testimony. The SEC is also investigating whether Nvidia’s disclosures misled investors. The scandal created uncertainty about whether Nvidia would continue Huang’s open-source push.
key_points: Interim CEO Collette Kress said Nvidia remains committed to a vibrant open-model ecosystem so countries, companies, and industries can build their own intelligence. The statement was meant to calm partners and developers after Jensen Huang’s departure, since Huang had been the company’s most visible advocate for open-source AI.

Kress cited a 35-fold year-over-year increase in weekly token volume on OpenRouter, including 3.5-fold growth in just three months. Nvidia uses the metric to argue open models are moving from experimentation to production, expanding demand for inference compute and strengthening the case for open-weight releases.

Nvidia’s $12.9 billion acquisition of Hugging Face is still expected to close. Hugging Face serves more than 118 million developers and 200,000 companies. Kress said Nvidia will scale the platform and make intelligence more open and accessible, though executives did not address the deal in the earnings Q&A.

Nvidia’s Nemotron family of open-weight models targets long-running agentic AI and reasoning workloads. Kress said Nemotron is now the most widely used U.S. open model on OpenRouter and is where developers start building their own intelligence, making it central to Nvidia’s open-source pitch.

Huang resigned after disclosures about extramarital affairs, including a relationship with an executive suspected of being a Chinese spy, and faces congressional testimony. The SEC is also investigating whether Nvidia’s disclosures misled investors. The scandal adds governance and legal risk even as Nvidia tries to show strategic continuity.
report.impact: Nvidia’s reassurances reduce immediate fears that the Hugging Face deal or Nemotron roadmap will be reversed, signaling that open weights remain a competitive strategy rather than a personal project of Huang. For the AI industry, a combined Nvidia-Hugging Face could tighten Nvidia’s grip on model distribution, tooling, and inference hardware, raising antitrust and ecosystem-lock-in questions. Developers may get better integrated tools and more open models, but should watch for platform dependence. Regular users could see more accessible AI products, though the leadership scandal and SEC probe may slow decisions and invite regulatory scrutiny. The token-growth data also suggests open-model demand is broad enough that Nvidia cannot easily retreat without ceding developer mindshare to rivals.
report.tools: Follow Hugging Face for open models and datasets, OpenRouter for cross-model routing and usage trends, and Nvidia’s Nemotron releases for open-weight agentic models. Developers can test deployment with Nvidia NeMo, TensorRT-LLM, and vLLM. Also track Nvidia’s regulatory filings and Hugging Face acquisition updates for strategy shifts. These are the key places to verify whether the open-source commitment holds.
